abstract: New atomic-layer nitridation process performed just after growth of InAs quantum dots produces red shift in the photoluminescence (PL) by more than 100 nm. Emission at >1.3 /spl mu/m was achieved at room temperature with no severe efficiency degradation.

articleTitle: Epitaxial wafer quality versus substrate quality
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: The effect of various InP substrates properties on epitaxial layer quality was investigated. From the results of experiments on MOCVD, we found that the average haze of epitaxial layer surfaces measured by surfscan can be reduced by using substrates with optimum surface mis-orientation angles of 0.05-0.10 degrees. Our experiments on MBE also showed a similar tendency. Furthermore it was found that appropriate treatment of substrates prevents slips on the periphery of epitaxial wafers.

articleTitle: Topological characteristics of MBE grown Sb-introduced Ga(In)As covered InAs quantum dots on GaAs
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We found the size enlargement of MBE grown InAs quantum dot (QD) on GaAs using a Sb-introduced Ga(In)As cover layer for the first time. The effect of the GaInAsSb cover layer on topological properties of QDs was investigated for various indium (In) and antimony (Sb) compositions in cover layers by atomic force microscopy (AFM). Elongation of the PL wavelength was confirmed as the result of increase of the QD height with reduced lateral size.

articleTitle: Tungsten buried growth by using thin flow-liner for small collector capacitance in InP HBT
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: To realize small C/sub BC/, condition of buried growth of tungsten wire in InP was studied. By increase of flow speed (50 cm/s to 3 m/s), HBT with tungsten wire showed small C/sub BC/ (0.6 fF).

articleTitle: Regenerative wavelength conversion using optical flip-flop outputs of multimode interference bistable laser diodes
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Regenerative wavelength conversion was obtained using multimode interference bistable laser diodes and cross gain saturation in semiconductor optical amplifiers. A digital transfer function of wavelength conversion was achieved through the optical flip-flop thresholding function

articleTitle: Influence of strain-compensating and strain-mediating layers on the optical properties of MOVPE-grown GaInNAs single quantum-well structures
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: In summary, we have investigated the dependence of the optical properties of GaInNAs QWs grown by MOVPE on GaNAs SCLs and InGaAs SMLs. Introduction of only SCLs between the GaAs and GaInNAs QW deteriorates the epitaxial quality of the QW due to the increased stress between tensile-strained GaNAs and compressive-strained GaInNAs. This detrimental effect of the interface can be countered by the insertion of a layer of InGaAs. Contrary to what observed in MBE, MOVPE-grown GaInNAs QW with combined SCLs/SMLs demonstrated blue-shifted PL due to the decrease N content with improved QW quality.

articleTitle: Technology transfer of (Ga)InP-quantum dots
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We transferred the technology to grow (Ga)InP quantum dots from a home-built epitaxy MOVPE machine to a commercial machine. We were able to obtain quantum dots in our first runs proven by AFM and time-resolved photoluminescence

articleTitle: Design and analysis of MEMS tunable vertical-cavity semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We present revised widely-tunable vertical-cavity SOAs exhibiting a reduced tuning voltage and an increased wavelength tuning range. Additionally, detailed theoretical models have been developed and are shown to be in good agreement with experimental observations.

articleTitle: Low noise monolithic 40 GHz mode-locked DBR lasers based on GaInAsP/InP
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Very short optical pulses (1.2-2.0 ps) with low amplitude noise (0.8-2.0 %) and low timing jitter (<250 fs) over 5 nm wavelength tuning are reported from a monolithic 40 GHz mode-locked GaInAsP/InP laser

articleTitle: High resistivity in GaInP/GaAs by high temperature Fe ion implantation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We investigated the structural and electrical behavior of Fe implanted and annealed MOVPE grown GalnP layers lattice matched to GaAs substrates, demonstrating that high temperature Fe implantation can give rise to stable semi-insulating layers

articleTitle: MBE growth of InN and InGaN for 1 /spl mu/m wavelength optical device applications
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005

articleTitle: In-situ selective area etching by using HCl gas in an MOVPE reactor
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Aiming at improving the crystalline quality of a regrowth interface for integrated optical devices, we investigated in-situ gas etching in the selective area using hydrogen-chloride (HCl) gas with metalorganic vapor-phase epitaxy. The etching pattern at the mask edge was limited by (111)B and (100) planes. The depth of etching in the selective area can be controlled by the mask width and etching conditions. At a high etching temperature, the etching depth increases as the mask width is increased or the gap width is decreased. On the other hand, at a low etching temperature, etching depth is constant.

articleTitle: Copmparison of influence of rare earth elements and oxides on properties of InP for radiation detection
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We have focused on the investigation of the impact of Ce, Eu, Tm, EU<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and Tm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> addition in LPE growth process on the properties of InP layers in the context of their application in detector structures

articleTitle: Post-growth bandgap engineering in InP
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We report novel quantum-well intermixing techniques that allow multiple bandgaps to be generated on a single InP substrate or device. The proposed processes are suitable for the manufacture of monolithically integrated optoelectronic devices and circuits

articleTitle: InGaAs-InAlAs-InP HEMT technology for ultra-high frequency and ultra-low noise performance
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: InGaAs-InAlAs-InP HEMT is facing competition from the emerging MHEMT technology. Nonetheless, for top-performing applications requiring high gain and low noise, InP HEMT is still the preferred choice. We here present results from InP HEMT development for sub-100 nm gate length designs yielding f/sub max/ above 400 GHz and ultra-low noise hybrid amplifiers with a minimum noise temperature of 1.1 K when operated under cryogenic conditions.

articleTitle: Anomalous optical characteristics of InGaAsP on GaAs substrates grown by MOVPE
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: The mechanism of immiscibility of InGaAsP grown by MOVPE has been investigated. Anomalous optical characteristics which are related to the spinodal decomposition are revealed, and growth condition dependence of this phenomenon has been examined in detail.

articleTitle: Growth and characterization of 2" and 4" low EPD InP substrate crystals by the vertical gradient freeze (VGF)-method
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: The growth of twin-free 4" semi-insulating InP crystals is reported. The influence of the EPD of the seed crystal and the cone angle of the crucible on dislocation and twin formation were studied.

articleTitle: Technology development for photonic integration in InP
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We report our development activities towards high-density photonic integrated circuits. Two key technologies, quantum well intermixing and etched turning mirrors, are demonstrated in InGaAs/InAlGaAs InP-based material at a wavelength of 1.55 microns

articleTitle: Extremely low noise characteristics of 0.1/spl mu/m /spl Gamma/-gate power metamorphic HEMT on GaAs substrate
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: The 0.1 /spl mu/m /spl Gamma/-gate power metamorphic high electron mobility transistors (MHEMTs) has been fabricated and the DC, microwave, and noise performance of the device were characterized. The MHEMT device shows the DC output characteristics having an extrinsic transconductance of 830 mS/mm and a threshold voltage of /spl square/0.62 V. The f/sub T/ and f/sub max/ obtained for the 0.1 /spl mu/m/spl times/100 /spl mu/m MHEMT device are 165 GHz and 275 GHz, respectively. The MHEMTs exhibit the minimum noise figure, NF/sub min/, of 0.64 dB and associated gain of 12.4 dB at 26 GHz. The NF/sub min/ measured at 40 GHz is 1.1 dB with associated gain of 9.7 dB. This noise data is the lowest value ever reported for /spl Gamma/-gate power MHEMT devices with InGaAs channel of 53% In.

articleTitle: Spontaneous recombination lifetime in compressively strained InGaAs quantum well lasers with InGaAsP and GaAs barrier/waveguide layers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005

articleTitle: Effects of surface morphology and strain state of InAlGaP matrices on the growth of InP quantum dots by metalorganic chemical vapor deposition
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: InP self-assembled QDs were grown on InAlGaP matrices by MOCVD. Effects of the matrix surface morphology, the strain and its relaxation in the matrix on the morphology and luminescence properties of InP QDs were studied.

articleTitle: Thermal decomposition of indium phosphide: monitoring of metallic cluster growth
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: The formation and growth dynamics of differently prepared InP(001) surfaces before and after annealing and their influence upon the vibronic and electronic properties was investigated using various microscopic and spectroscopic techniques.

articleTitle: Fabrication of nanowires on InP(100) by Ar/sup +/ irradiation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Arrays of nanowires of 32 nm high, with a periodicity of 134 nm were produced over an area of several square micrometers with 2 keV Ar/sup +/ ion bombardment at 72/spl deg/ incidence angle to surface normal to a dose of 2/spl times/10/sup 17/ cm/sup -2/. The formation of ripples and nanowires is believed to arise from mergence of tailed cones agglomerated from In ions due to the preferential sputtering of P from InP.

articleTitle: Optical and structural characterization of InP nanorods
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: InP nanorods were chemically synthesized. We investigated the structures of InP nanorods and their optical properties by using UV-VIS spectroscopy, photoluminescence study, powder X-ray diffractometer and transmission electron microscopy. Also, we suggested their photonic applications.

articleTitle: Influence of Si/sub 3/N/sub 4/ passivation on electron mobility of InGaAs/InP composite channel high electron mobility transistor structures
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: The influence of silicon nitride passivation on electron mobility of InGaAs/InP composite channel high electron mobility transistor structures has been studied. An increase in effective mobility mu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> with a negligible change of sheet carrier density n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> after SiN deposition is clearly observed. Our results suggest that the enhancement of mu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> could be explained under the framework of electrons transfer from the InP sub-channel into InGaAs channel region due to the energy band bending at surface region caused by SiN passivation

articleTitle: Electrodeposited Pt/InP Schottky barriers with large barrier heights and large hydrogen sensitivity for sensor chips using InP-based uantum wire networks [uantum read quantum]
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Pt Schottky diodes were fabricated on n-InP by pulsed electrodeposition, and their H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> sensing properties were investigated. Deposition resulted in formation of Pt nanoparticles. As compared with diodes by vacuum deposition, electrodeposited diodes gave much higher Schottky barrier heights (SBHs) of 810 meV. They showed marked increase of the reverse current on exposure to H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas in air. The magnitudes of current change and on-off transients depended on the partial pressure of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. The detection mechanism is explained in terms of SBH change caused by adsorption/desorption of atomic hydrogen at the Pt/semiconductor interface. Its behavior was strongly affected by the presence of oxygen in the atmosphere. Integration of the present sensor with a hexagonal quantum wire network is proposed for realization of a wireless hydrogen sensor chip

articleTitle: Deep levels characterization in high temperature iron implanted InP
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We have investigated the electrical activation of Fe implanted in InP in different concentrations and we have characterized by DLTS and by C-V analyses the electrical activity of the deep levels present in the band gap.

articleTitle: Room temperature CW operation of InAs/InP (100) quantum dots based buried ridge stripe lasers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Fabrication of InAs QDs grown on (100) InP substrate by GSMBE is reported. We investigate the room temperature operation of QDs-based broad area and buried ridge stripe lasers emitting at 1.5 /spl mu/m (J/sub Th/, T/sub 0/, /spl alpha//sub H/).

articleTitle: Emission tuning from a fiber-coupled GaInNAs VCSEL
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We report the single-mode operation and characteristics of a 1.3-/spl mu/m fiber-coupled tunable GaInNAs VCSEL for different pump wavelengths. Results shows that the device can be continuously tuned over 18.5-nm with output power up to 0.23-mW.

articleTitle: InP based ballistic nanodevices
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: The paper presents the state of the art and the future trends in the field of AlInAs/GaInAs/InP based nanometre devices, in particular ballistic T junctions and plasma wave transistors.

articleTitle: Low threshold current 1540 nm wavelength GaInAsP/InP quantum-wire distributed-feedback lasers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: 1540 nm wavelength GaInAsP/InP quantum-wire (24 nm wide) distributed feedback lasers were realized by dry etching and regrowth method. A threshold current as low as 2.7 mA, a differential quantum efficiency of 19 %/facet and an SMSR of 51 dB (@ 2I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sub>) were attained under RT-CW condition for the stripe width of 3.0 mum and the cavity length of 330 mum

articleTitle: Growth-temperature-dependent bandgap of MBE-grown GaInNAs epilayers lattice matched to GaAs
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We have observed that the bandgap of lattice-matched GaInNAs-on-GaAs epilayers, grown by molecular beam epitaxy under constant fluxes, noticeably increases as growth temperature increases within the 410-470degC range. The increase in the band gap with increasing growth temperature has been found to be due to a decrease in the substitutional nitrogen content as well as to an enhancement in the amount of N-Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>In clusters relative to the N-Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> ones

articleTitle: Study of photoluminescence and deep-level defects in Be-doped InGaAsN
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We have investigated the temperature-dependent photoluminescence and deep-level defects in Be-doped, p-type In/sub 0.03/Ga/sub 0.97/As/sub 0.99/N/sub 0.01/ grown by radio frequency plasma-assisted solid source molecular beam epitaxy.

articleTitle: Development of 1550 nm bipolar cascade lasers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Operation of a 1550 nm, single mode, bipolar cascade laser is demonstrated. Differential quantum efficiency of 86% at room temperature was obtained from two MQW active regions connected in series by a novel tunnel junction.

articleTitle: Selective area MOVPE based InP WDM channel selector
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We demonstrate an integrated channel selector featuring an array of quantum well semiconductor optical amplifiers and arrayed waveguide demultiplexer. 12 dB crosstalk was achieved, first ever for a device using single selective area MOVPE.

articleTitle: Electronic and optical properties of copper doped InP single crystals
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Annealed wafers of Czochralski grown copper doped InP were investigated by temperature dependent Hall measurements and low-temperature Fourier transform infrared absorption. New peaks around 2100 cm/sup -1/ were interpreted as due to Cu/sup 2+/ 3d internal transitions.

articleTitle: 0.1/spl mu/m InGaAs/InAlAs/InP HEMT low noise amplifiers with compact stacked cascode design and its de-bias effect induced failure (DBIF)
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Compact Q-band low noise amplifier modules using 0.1 /spl mu/m InGaAs/InAlAs/InP HEMT MMICs have been demonstrated with high performance and high manufacturability over a frequency band from 43.5 to 45.5 GHz at Northrop Grumman Space Technology (NGST). The compact InP HEMT LNAs and modules are essential for phased-array applications. The LNA modules demonstrate noise figure less than 2.5 dB over the frequency band of 43.5 to 45.5 GHz. The RF performance results achieved here, in conjunction with previously reported high reliability results, further demonstrate the readiness of NGST's 0.1 /spl mu/m InP HEMT MMIC technology for advanced phased-array applications. In addition, Ig de-bias effect induced failure (DBIF) was observed on InP HEMT MMICs with stacked cascode configuration subjected to elevated temperature lifetest. Accordingly, an acceptable lifetest temperature window was found to alleviate DBIF while performing lifetest on InP HEMT MMICs with stacked cascode configuration.

articleTitle: Study of the defects in InP:Fe using time-resolved reflection spectroscopy
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: The photo-excited carrier dynamics in Fe doped InP using time-resolved differential reflection measurement. Considering the influence of the ambipolar and surface recombination velocity on carrier dynamics, the temporal evolution of photo-excited carrier has also investigated. In addition, the measurement of transient photoluminescence is employed.

articleTitle: 5 km nearly dispersion penalty free transmission of FP lasers at 10 Gb/s and 85/spl deg/C
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Dispersion penalty free transmission at 5 km, 85/spl deg/C, and 10 Gb/s was demonstrated using AlGaInAs FP lasers, through careful spectral management, laser material and structure optimization. These optimized devices demonstrated lasing to over 120/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Wavelength conversion using polarization dependence of cross-phase modulation in an InGaAlAs multiple-quantum-well electroabsorption modulator
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate wavelength conversion using polarization dependence of cross-phase-modulation in an InGaAlAs MQW-EA modulator that can operate at small signal power less than +8 dBm and give very high extinction ratio over 31 dB.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo investigation of voltage-current characteristic nonlinearity and harmonic generation in submicron semiconductor structures
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Using a Monte-Carlo code, self-consistently coupled with a one-dimensional Poisson-solver, we simulate the nonlinear carrier dynamics in InP n+nn+ structures operating under large-amplitude periodic signals and investigate the voltage-current hysteresis cycle and the high-order-harmonic generation.

articleTitle: Highest density 1.3 /spl mu/m InAs quantum dots covered with gradient composition InGaAs SRL grown with an As/sub 2/ source using molecular beam epitaxy
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We propose a GaAs-based 1.3 /spl mu/m InAs quantum dot (QD) structure for optical devices that uses a novel gradient composition strain reducing layer (GC-SRL) and dimeric arsenic (As/sub 2/). Our proposed GC-SRL has a big advantage, such as reducing critical strain. We calculate the critical thickness of InGaAs GC-SRL for several In compositions. Also, The characteristics of 1.3 /spl mu/m InAs QDs that employ AS/sub 2/ are different from those of QDs that use AS/sub 4/. Our optimum structure exhibits the first room temperature emission of over 1.3 /spl mu/m with a linewidth of 22 meV and a high density of over 1.1/spl times/10/sup 11/ cm/sup -2/ using only a GC-SRL. We were also able to achieve a very high density of 3.3/spl times/ 10/sup 11/ cm/sup -2/ and a full width at half maximum of 23 meV for a triple-stack structure within the critical thickness. This result is promising as regards achieving a semiconductor laser and the other optical devices with QDs of over 1.3 /spl mu/m on a GaAs substrate for use in fiber communications.

articleTitle: Single mode performance and structural quality of MOVPE grown InP based quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We report single longitudinal mode, T>300 K operation of MOVPE-grown InGaAs/AlInAs DFB quantum cascade lasers. Structural investigation indicates the epitaxial quality of the active region to be equivalent to high performing MBE grown structures.

articleTitle: Extended operating temperature range of passively mode locked laser diode based on adaptable saturable absorber design
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We report passive mode locking operation of phosphorus quaternary based laser diodes at high operating temperatures. With an adapted design of the absorber, stable mode locking is observed at temperatures of up to 75 C

articleTitle: Optimizing lateral HBT design by utilizing performance estimations
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: In this work, we concentrate on the fundamental relations for improving the HBT device performance by varying the layout and general transistor design parameters. With respect to the widely known analytical equations for the HBT device behavior, estimations have been made to predict the optimum design. These estimations have been proven by fabricating a large number of different designs on the same wafer. In this paper, the dependence on emitter length and width dimensions will be in focus, as well as general orientation issues

articleTitle: Above room temperature operation of injectorless quantum-cascade lasers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We present an injectorless quantum-cascade laser with significantly reduced threshold-current densities and a maximum operating temperature of 350 K. The wavelength is 10 /spl mu/m at 77 K and 8.4 /spl mu/m at 300 K.

articleTitle: Electro-optic sampling using wide-band high-efficiency ion-irradiated photoconductor as optical-to-electrical converter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We propose a new version of electro-optic sampler at 1.5 mum, which uses an ion-irradiated InP-based photoconductor for the optical-to-electrical conversion. A measurement bandwidth larger than 300 GHz is obtained for a signal-to-noise ratio higher than 15 dB and excitation pulses of peak amplitude as high as 0.81 V. The performances of our system are validated from test measurements performed on coplanar waveguide transmission lines made on semi-insulating InP substrates

articleTitle: MOCVD process modeling using in-situ reflectance test structure measurements for process control improvement
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: Process control methodology based on in-situ reflectance measurements can be used with a process model to reduce calibration runs in the development and manufacture of InGaAlAs lasers and modulators.

articleTitle: Design and performance of InP/GaInAs/InP abrupt DHBTs
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We discuss the field collapse threshold in abrupt DHBTs in which the barrier between the base and the collector is eliminated by delta doping. A DHBT with 150 nm thick collector operating at a current density of 4 mA/mum<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is presented. We show theoretically that the carrier density at the onset of the filed collapse effect can be doubled by inserting an additional delta doped layer at the center of the collector

articleTitle: Prediction method for the bandgap profiles of InGaAsP multiple quantum well structures fabricated by selective area metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We simulated the bandgap distribution of InGaAsP MQWs grown by selective-area MOVPE based on vapor-phase diffusion model. The accuracy of the simulation was sufficient for the design of integrated semiconductor optical devices

articleTitle: Mid-infrared InAs-based quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: We report our recent experimental results on mid-infrared InAs-based quantum cascade lasers grown on n-InAs(100) substrates by molecular beam epitaxy. An InAs double plasmon waveguide is used for the optical confinement. The completed QCLs operate at 8-14 /spl mu/m wavelength range. Observed minimum threshold current density at 80 K by using InAs/AlGaSb superlattice active layers is 0.42 kA/cm/sup 2/, which is the lowest threshold current density in the mid-infrared region. The observed maximum operation temperature is 270 K.

articleTitle: Self-aligned InP DHBTs for 150 GHz digital and mixed signal circuits
publicationTitle: International Conference on Indium Phosphide and Related Materials, 2005
abstract: A production oriented manufacturing process for Indium Phosphide double-heterojunction bipolar transistor (DHBT) devices that enables 150 GHz digital and mixed signal circuits is presented. These transistors have cut-off frequency (f) and maximum oscillation frequency (f/sub max/) both over 300 GHz and open-base breakdown voltage (BV/sub ceo/) over 4 V. Common Mode Logic (CML) ring oscillators have exhibited 1.95 ps gate delay and Emitter Coupled Logic (ECL) static frequency dividers that operate up to 152 GHz have been demonstrated to benchmark this InP process technology. A 4:1 multiplexer for 100 Gb/s circuits is discussed along with a Gilbert cell Variable Gain Amplifier with excess of 50 GHz bandwidth and record gain bandwidth product of 397 GHz.
